statement: Annotated from the Beinecke scan alone (canvas 1006250, the part of the f101v foldout that carries this page's text; the adjoining scan 1006251 shows the next opening and was used only to check where this page ends). No transcription word and no other annotation of this folio was read. The page is a tall pharmaceutical page with the text in one ten-line paragraph at the foot and drawings above it in two bands. Four red jars with pale rims and dark neck bands stand down the left margin: upper, upper-middle, lower-middle and bottom. The upper band holds two rows: a tree-like plant with rounded green leaves on a pale trunk, a fern-like plant with pinnate leaves and an orange root, a star-leaved plant with a pale forked stem and two pale roots, and a tall ivy-leaved plant at the upper right; then a large round green leaf on a long curled stem, a plant with broad green leaves and a red root, a large fan-shaped leaf with a red root, and a spiny star-leaved plant at the right. The lower band holds a tall segmented spiky plant with a red root, a plant with broad green leaves and two blue flowers, a fan-leaved plant with a red root, a plant with rounded lobed leaves on branching stems whose root is drawn with a face, and a narrow spiky plant at the right edge. The transcription has eighteen label lines on this folio ; I could not tie an individual locus to an individual object from the scan's layout with confidence, because several label lines stand between two drawings at once, so every label is recorded null rather than guessed. The objects are listed in reading order, left to right and top to bottom.
